verses.text: When Pentecost arrived, all the believers were gathered together in one place.
Suddenly, a sound came from heaven like a strong wind rushing through. It filled the whole house where they were sitting.
They saw what looked like tongues of fire separating and settling on each one of them. 🔥
All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began speaking in other languages, as the Spirit gave them the words.
At that time, devout Jewish people from every nation under heaven were living in Jerusalem.
When they heard the sound, a crowd gathered. They were confused, because each person heard the believers speaking in their own language.
They were amazed and said to each other, “Aren’t all these speakers from Galilee?
How is it that each of us hears them speaking in our own native language?
We’re Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and people from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, and parts of Libya near Cyrene. Some of us came from Rome—Jewish people and converts to Judaism.
Some are from Crete, others from Arabia, and we hear them speaking in our own languages about God’s mighty works!”
They were all amazed and confused, asking each other, “What does this mean?”
But others made fun of them: “They’ve had too much new wine.”
Then Peter stood up with the eleven apostles, raised his voice, and said, “People of Judea and everyone living in Jerusalem, hear me out and understand this.
These people aren’t drunk, as you think. It’s only the third hour of the day.
What you’re seeing is what God spoke through the prophet Joel:
“In the last days, God says, I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy. Your young people will see visions, and your elders will dream dreams.
Even on my male and female servants, I will pour out my Spirit in those days, and they will prophesy.
I will show wonders in the sky above and signs on the earth below: blood, fire, and clouds of smoke.
The sun will turn dark, and the moon will look like blood before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.
Then everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”
“People of Israel, listen to this: Jesus of Nazareth was shown to be from God among you through the mighty works, wonders, and signs God did through him. You saw it yourselves.
Jesus was handed over according to God’s plan and foreknowledge. You used lawless people to nail him to a cross and kill him.
But God raised him up, freeing him from death’s agony, because death could not hold him.
David said about him: “I always saw the Lord before me. He is at my right hand, so I won’t be shaken.
That’s why my heart is glad and my words are full of joy. Even my body will rest in hope,
because you will not abandon me to the realm of the dead or let your Holy One decay.
You’ve shown me the paths of life; your presence will fill me with joy.”
“Brothers and sisters, I can speak plainly to you about our ancestor David. He died, was buried, and his tomb is still here among us.
David was a prophet. He knew God had sworn to him that one of his own descendants would be raised up as the Messiah to sit on his throne.
So David saw ahead and spoke about the Messiah’s resurrection. He would not be abandoned to the place of the dead, and his body would not decay.
God raised this Jesus to life, and we are all witnesses of it.
Now Jesus has been lifted up to God’s right hand. He received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit and has poured out what you now see and hear.
David himself did not go up into heaven, yet he said: “The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at my right hand
until I make your enemies a footstool under your feet.’”
“So all Israel should know this for certain: God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.”
When the people heard this, it hit them in the heart. They asked Peter and the other apostles, “Brothers, what should we do?”
Peter answered, “Turn back to God, and each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. You will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
This promise is for you, your children, and everyone far away—as many as the Lord our God calls to himself.”
Peter kept speaking and urged them with many other words: “Get yourselves out of this crooked generation!”
Those who welcomed his message were baptized. About three thousand people joined the believers that day.
They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching, sharing life together, breaking bread, and praying.
A sense of awe came over everyone, and the apostles did many wonders and signs.
All the believers stayed together and shared what they had.
They sold their property and possessions and shared the money with anyone who had a need.
Day after day, they met together in the temple. They broke bread in their homes and shared meals with glad, generous hearts.
They praised God and were respected by all the people. Every day the Lord added to their community those who were being saved.
